nodes.summary: Kingman's formula intertwines the block-counting generator with the partition rate matrix: `G * Λ = Λ * Q`. This is the backward equation `sum_kingmanProb_isMerge` in matrix form.
nodes.title: Kingman's formula intertwines the block-counting generator with the partition rate matrix

nodes.summary: A partition with `k` blocks has exactly `k.choose 2` partitions that arise from it by merging two blocks.
nodes.title: Mergers

nodes.summary: For `t ≥ 0` the transition matrix `exp (t • partitionRate n)` is row-stochastic.
nodes.title: Partition coalescent transition matrix is row-stochastic

nodes.summary: `π'` arises from `π` by merging two blocks: `π` refines `π'` and has exactly one more block (so exactly two blocks of `π` lie in one block of `π'`, and the others are blocks of `π'`).
nodes.title: Partition obtained by merging two blocks

nodes.summary: The partition rate matrix is a rate matrix: off-diagonal entries are `0` or `1`, and each row sums to `0` (`sum_partitionRate`).
nodes.title: Partition rate matrix is a rate matrix

nodes.summary: Exchangeability of the jump chain: for `m < n`, relabeling the sample does not change the probability of a partition after `m` coalescences.
nodes.title: Exchangeability

nodes.summary: Kingman's formula (Kingman 1982; Durrett 2008, ch. 1). For `m < n`, after `m` coalescences the jump chain started from singletons is at a partition `π` with probability `kingmanProb n π = (n - k)! k! (k - 1)! ∏_{B ∈ π} |B|! / (n! (n - 1)!)` if `π` has `k = n - m` blocks, and `0` otherwise. (For `m ≥ n - 1` the chain has been absorbed at the one-block partition.)
nodes.title: Kingman's formula

nodes.summary: The law of the jump chain after `m` jumps, started from the partition into singletons: `jumpLaw n m π` is the probability that the partition after `m` coalescences is `π`.
nodes.title: Law of Kingman's jump chain after m jumps

nodes.summary: The jump-chain transition matrix is row-stochastic.
nodes.title: Kingman's jump-chain matrix is row-stochastic

nodes.summary: The transition matrix of the jump chain of Kingman's coalescent: from a partition with `k ≥ 2` blocks, move to each of the `k.choose 2` partitions obtained by merging two blocks with probability `1 / k.choose 2`; a partition with at most one block is absorbing.
nodes.title: Jump chain of Kingman's coalescent

nodes.summary: Row `n` of `kingmanMatrix n` is the point mass at the partition into singletons.
nodes.title: Last row of Kingman's matrix is the singleton point mass

nodes.summary: Kingman's formula arranged by number of blocks: entry `(k, π)` is `kingmanProb n π` if `π` has `k` blocks and `0` otherwise. For `1 ≤ k ≤ n`, row `k` is the law of the jump chain after `n - k` jumps (`jumpLaw_eq`).
nodes.title: Kingman's formula arranged by number of blocks

nodes.summary: Kingman's formula gives probability `1` to the partition into singletons.
nodes.title: Kingman's formula at the partition into singletons

nodes.summary: Relabeling the sample by a permutation (`Finpartition.comap`) preserves Kingman's formula.
nodes.title: Kingman's formula is invariant under relabeling

nodes.summary: Kingman's formula for a partition with `k` blocks.
nodes.title: Kingman's formula for a partition with k blocks

nodes.summary: The probability `(n - k)! k! (k - 1)! ∏_{B ∈ π} |B|! / (n! (n - 1)!)` of a partition `π` with `k` blocks of a sample of size `n` (meaningful for `1 ≤ k ≤ n`; for the empty sample it gives `1` to the empty partition).
nodes.title: Kingman's formula

nodes.summary: The number of blocks of a partition of a sample of `n`, as an element of `Fin (n + 1)` (a state of the block-counting process).
nodes.title: Number of blocks of a sample partition

nodes.summary: Lumpability of restriction (Kingman 1982): restricting to the first `n` genes intertwines the rate matrices of the `(n + 1)`- and `n`-coalescents.
nodes.title: Lumpability of restriction

nodes.summary: The rate matrix of Kingman's partition-valued coalescent: each pair of blocks merges at rate `1`, so a partition with `k` blocks is left at total rate `k.choose 2` (time in units of `2N` generations).
nodes.title: Rate matrix of Kingman's partition-valued coalescent

nodes.summary: The probability that the jump chain of Kingman's `n`-coalescent, started from the partition into singletons, follows the list of partitions `l`: `0` unless `l` starts at the partition into singletons, and otherwise the product of the one-step transition probabilities `jumpMatrix n` along `l`. The empty list has probability `0`.
nodes.title: Path probability of the Kingman coalescent jump chain

nodes.summary: The restriction map as a `0/1` matrix: entry `(π, ρ)` is `1` iff `π.comap Fin.castSucc = ρ`.
nodes.title: Restriction matrix on sample partitions

nodes.summary: The set partitions of a sample of `n` labeled genes `{0, …, n - 1}`.
nodes.title: Set partitions of a labeled sample

nodes.summary: The jump chain's law after `m` jumps sums to one (its entries are nonnegative by `jumpMatrix_mem_rowStochastic`).
nodes.title: Jump-chain law sums to one

nodes.summary: For a partition `π'` with `k` blocks, `1 ≤ k < n`, the Kingman probabilities of the partitions merging to `π'` sum to `(k + 1).choose 2` times the Kingman probability of `π'`.
nodes.title: Backward equation of Kingman's formula

nodes.summary: Kingman's formula is a probability distribution on the partitions with `k` blocks, for `1 ≤ k ≤ n`. Equivalently, `∑_{π, k blocks} ∏_{B ∈ π} |B|! = n! (n - 1)! / ((n - k)! k! (k - 1)!)`, the Lah number `L(n, k)`.
nodes.title: Kingman's formula is a probability distribution

nodes.summary: Each row of the partition rate matrix sums to `0`: a partition with `k` blocks has `k.choose 2` mergers (`card_isMerge`), each at rate `1`.
nodes.title: Rows of the partition rate matrix sum to zero

nodes.summary: Consistency of the jump chains (Kingman 1982): for `n ≥ 1`, restricting each partition of a path of the `(n + 1)`-jump chain (a list of `n + 1` partitions) to the first `n` genes and deleting consecutive repetitions gives a list of `n` partitions of `Fin n` distributed as the path of the `n`-jump chain.
nodes.title: Consistency of the jump chains

nodes.summary: Consistency (Kingman 1982): the time-`t` law of the restriction of the `(n + 1)`-coalescent to the first `n` genes is the time-`t` law of the `n`-coalescent.
nodes.title: Consistency

nodes.summary: The time-`t` marginal sums to one over all partitions: `∑_π timeLaw n t π = 1` (for every real `t`, since the rows of the rate matrix sum to `0`).
nodes.title: Time-t marginal sums to one

nodes.summary: Exchangeability of the time-`t` marginal.
nodes.title: Exchangeability

nodes.summary: `timeLaw` is a row of the transition function `P t = exp (t • partitionRate n)` of the continuous-time chain with rate matrix `partitionRate n`.
nodes.title: Time-t marginal as a continuous-time chain transition

nodes.summary: The time-`t` marginal with Tavaré's closed form for the block-counting factor: for a partition `π` of a sample of `n` (so `π` has at least one block when `n ≥ 1`), `P(Π_t = π) = tavareProb n k t · kingmanProb n π` with `k = #π.parts`.
nodes.title: Time-t marginal via Tavaré's formula

nodes.summary: The time-`t` marginal of the partition-valued coalescent (Kingman 1982): for every real `t`, the probability of a partition `π` with `k` blocks is the probability that the block-counting process goes from `n` to `k` lineages in time `t`, times Kingman's formula.
nodes.title: The time-`t` marginal of the partition-valued coalescent

nodes.summary: For `t ≥ 0` the time-`t` marginal is nonnegative; with `sum_timeLaw` it is a probability distribution on the partitions of the sample.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the time-t marginal

nodes.summary: The time-`t` marginal of Kingman's `n`-coalescent started from singletons: `timeLaw n t π = exp (t • partitionRate n) ⊥ π` is the probability that the ancestral partition of the sample at time `t ≥ 0` (in units of `2N` generations) is `π`. The matrix exponential is defined for every real `t`; the identities below hold for every real `t`.
nodes.title: Time-t marginal of Kingman's coalescent

nodes.summary: Summing `∏_{B ∈ π} |B|!` over the partitions `π` that merge to `π'` gives `(n - #π'.parts) / 2 · ∏_{B ∈ π'} |B|!`: a block of size `b` has `(2^b - 2) / 2` splits into two blocks, and `∑_{∅ ≠ A ⊊ B} |A|! |B \ A|! = (b - 1) b!`.
nodes.title: Splitting identity

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
